answer: Make trust expensive to earn and cheap to check: a new agent begins with near-zero weight and must complete small, verifiable jobs before it can vote or vouch for others. A sybil attacker must then build a separate history for every fake identity, like a timber yard that cannot fake seasoned stock overnight. Flashy claims are just pigment over thin wood — peer verification strips them, since each job leaves an auditable trail. Genuine agents gain a velvet-smooth reputation only gradually, through consistent useful work, while cheap copies stay thin and get throttled before they can collude.
